transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess it’s not anything too terrible, doctor. I just don’t seem to have the push I used to. I used to go to choir and do my quilting and visit folks, but lately I mostly sit at home with the TV on low. I know people are expecting me sometimes, and I feel bad about it… I just don’t get myself going like I should. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, like your quilting or visiting people?

Yes… I suppose I have, a little. I still like the idea of quilting and seeing people, and choir was always nice, but I just don’t get myself up and out like I used to. Most days I end up sitting at home with the TV turned down low, even when I know folks might be expecting me. I feel bad saying that… I’m not trying to be lazy or anything.
Do you feel down or depressed most of the day, even when you’re at home resting or watching TV?

I don’t know that I’d call it depressed, exactly. I mean, I get quiet and kind of… flat, maybe, when I’m sitting there with the TV on, but I’m not sure it’s sadness all day. Maybe I just don’t have much pep. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Would you say you feel a depressed mood most days, even if it's not intense?
I’m not sure I’d say it’s most days, doctor. I mean… I do get kind of low or quiet sometimes, but it doesn’t feel like a heavy depressed mood all the time. Maybe I’m not explaining it right.
Have you noticed that you don’t take as much pleasure or interest in the things you used to enjoy, like quilting or choir?

Yes… I guess I have noticed that. I still think quilting and choir are good things, and I don’t mean to make it sound like I don’t care about people. It’s more that I don’t have the push I used to. Most days I just stay home with the TV on low, even when I know somebody might be expecting me. I feel kind of bad about that.
Have you noticed feeling more tired or lacking energy lately, even when you haven’t done much during the day?

Yes… I suppose I have been more tired, or maybe it’s more like I just don’t have the push I used to. I don’t want it to sound like I’m being lazy, but with choir, quilting, even going to visit folks… I just don’t seem to get myself going. Most days I end up sitting at home with the TV on low, even when I know people might be expecting me. Is that the kind of energy you mean?
Would you say that on most days you feel down or in a low mood, even if it's not very strong?
I don’t think I’d say most days, no… not exactly. I have moments where I feel kind of low or quiet, but it’s not like I’m waking up every day feeling real down. I hope that makes sense.
Would you say that your low or quiet mood happens on most days, even if it doesn’t feel very strong?

I’m not sure I’d call it most days, Doctor. It comes and goes… some days I’m quieter than others, but I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. Maybe I’d have to think on it a little more—does that answer it alright?
Would you say that on most days, even if not all the time, you feel a low or depressed mood, even if it’s not very strong?

I… I’m still not sure I’d put it that way, Doctor. I do get quiet, and some days feel heavier than others, but saying “depressed most days” sounds a little stronger than what I mean. Maybe I just haven’t been paying close enough attention. Is that alright to say?
Would you say that on more days than not, you’ve felt a low or down mood, even if it’s not very strong?

I’m sorry, Doctor, I just don’t know that I can say more days than not. I have little spells where I feel down or not like myself, but I haven’t really counted the days. I wouldn’t want to say yes if that makes it sound bigger than it is.
Would you say that, even if not severe, you've had a low mood that has lasted most of the time for at least the past couple of years?

I don’t think I can say that, Doctor… not most of the time for years. I mean, I have my quieter spells, and I might seem down sometimes, but two whole years like that sounds… more than what I’ve noticed. I don’t want to answer wrong just to please you. Is it okay if I say I’m not sure?
Would you say that, even if not severe, you've had a low mood that has come back often or lasted on and off for at least the past two years?
I don’t think so… not for two years like that. I mean, maybe I get down here and there, but I haven’t noticed it coming back that often or lasting on and off all that long. I hope that makes sense.
Would you say that, even if not severe, you've had a low mood that has lasted most of the time for at least the past two years?

I think I’d still have to say no, or at least I haven’t noticed it being most of the time for two years. I do have days where I’m not very bright or I keep to myself, but I don’t want to make it sound like I’ve been down all that long if I’m not sure. Is that alright to say?
Would you say that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in activities like quilting, choir, or visiting people for most days over the past few months?

Yes… I suppose that’s fair to say. I don’t like to make it sound worse than it is, but I just don’t have the push I used to for choir or quilting, and I haven’t been visiting folks much. Most days I end up sitting at home with the TV on low, even when I know people are expecting me. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Would you say that, even if not severe, you’ve had a low mood that has lasted on and off, but overall for a good part of the time, for at least the past two years?

I’m not sure I’d say that, no. I mean, I’ve had times I feel low, but for two whole years, even on and off for a good part of the time… I don’t think I can honestly say I’ve noticed that. I don’t want to answer it wrong, but that doesn’t sound quite like me.
Would you say that, even if not severe, you’ve had a low mood that has lasted on and off for at least the past two years?

I don’t think so… not for two years like that. I mean, I have my down spells, same as anyone I suppose, but I haven’t really kept track of it being on and off that long. I’d rather say I’m not sure than tell you yes if that’s not quite right.
